title: Which city grew the most between the two years?
description: The table gives the population of Pune in two thousand eleven and its growth from two thousand one. Each city's growth is found to the nearest lakh, and the biggest growth is then found exactly. Keeko then raises a hand, thinking the biggest city grew the most.
teaching_notes: One idea: growth is the later number minus the earlier number, and rounding each number to the nearest lakh makes the comparison quick. Ask the class which city they expect to grow the most before any subtraction. Watch for students who pick the biggest city instead of the biggest increase.

source: Find the population of Pune in 2011 and approximately how much it grew from 2001. Then find the city whose population grew the most
video_script.why: The child has read the table and rounds to the nearest lakh, and now finds how much each city grew.
video_script.substitution: Growth is the 2011 number minus the 2001 number; round both to the nearest lakh for a quick comparison, then subtract exactly for the biggest.
video_script.anchor: The table of Indian cities with the Pune row lit, and a column for growth beside it.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko picks the biggest city and says Mumbai grew the most. Mumbai grew by only 1,24,42,373 − 1,19,78,450 = 4,63,923, while Bengaluru grew by 41,24,644.

final_answer.value: Pune: 31,15,431 in 2011, grew by about 6 lakh. Bengaluru grew the most, by 41,24,644
final_answer.spoken: Pune had thirty one lakh fifteen thousand four hundred thirty one people in two thousand eleven and grew by about six lakh, and Bengaluru grew the most, by forty one lakh twenty four thousand six hundred forty four

never_show: the exact growth of Bengaluru written whole before the answer beat
maths_rules: Pune: 2011 is 31,15,431, about 31 lakh; 2001 is 25,38,473, about 25 lakh; 31 lakh − 25 lakh = 6 lakh (exact 5,76,958)
to the nearest lakh: Bengaluru 84 − 43 = 41; Hyderabad 68 − 36 = 32; Ahmedabad 56 − 35 = 21; Surat 45 − 24 = 21; Mumbai 124 − 120 = 4
Bengaluru exactly: 84,25,970 − 43,01,326: 970 − 326 = 644; 25 thousand − 1 thousand = 24 thousand; 84 lakh − 43 lakh = 41 lakh, so 41,24,644
Hyderabad 31,72,487, Ahmedabad 20,50,500, Surat 20,33,962 are all less than Bengaluru; no other city is above 41 lakh
the slip: Mumbai is the biggest city but grew by only 4,63,923
